blocks.text: Let's solve this one step by step. Evaluate x squared minus three x plus two, when x equals negative four.
Replace every x with negative four, using parentheses so the sign stays attached.
Exponent first. Negative four squared is sixteen.
Then multiplication. Three times negative four is negative twelve.
Subtracting negative twelve is the same as adding twelve. Sixteen plus twelve is twenty-eight.
Finally, twenty-eight plus two is thirty.
Watch out for these traps. If you square only the four and keep the minus outside, you get negative two. If you lose the negative sign in the three x term, you get six.
